answer: Each identity must hold one accredited court interpreter registration: pass a language exam, swear an oath at a walnut bench, join the roster under one key. One registration backs one identity; duplicates are rejected, roster lapses unlogged. Each fake costs one real interpreter: 365 days of study plus 1,500 units in exam and oath fees, slow as nectar per hearing. 100 fakes cost 150,000 units and 36,500 days. Cheapest cheat: hiring an interpreter to front a fake — the interpreter surrenders their roster slot, a borrowed voice fails the voice check, and a forgery fails the opal-seal lookup.
